title: Test-rig commissioning measurements
machine: Test rig: 3-axis DIY wooden-frame router. Zhulong V2.0 board (Mesa 7i92 derivative, hm2_eth, HAL prefix hm2_7i92.0), TB6560 drivers, Japan Servo KH42KM2 NEMA 17 motors (200 steps/rev), LinuxCNC 2.9.10 live USB.
notes: Raw numbers from the commissioning session on the rig, phases ('Faz') 1-8. Keys starting computed_ are arithmetic on the recorded numbers (formula given), not further measurements; keys ending _approx were recorded as 'about'. Axis keys are x, y, z. 'Session frame' = unhomed joint positions in that LinuxCNC session, before homing. 'Machine frame' = after homing: origin at the home switch's latch release edge, HOME_OFFSET 0. The INI comments cite this file as 'JSON'. The PC's LAN address is deliberately not recorded (deploy/machine.local, git-ignored).

faz1_y_dir.notes: Y has two motors on two TB6560 drivers. With both drivers on AXIS 1 (stepgen.01) neither ever changed direction: the 'Y DIR fault'. The levels compare the shared AXIS 1 with X's single-driver AXIS 0. Cause: one 3.3 V output cannot drive two optocouplers. Fix: Y's second driver moved to AXIS 3 = stepgen.03; the HAL end block mirrors stepgen.01's [JOINT_1] settings onto stepgen.03. Gate 1 passed.
faz1_y_dir.levels_notes: dir_low was recorded only for X's single-driver AXIS 0 ('DIR low 0.2 V', next to the DIR-high comparison).
faz1_y_dir.cause: one 3.3 V output cannot drive two optocouplers

fix.hal: configs/test-rig/test-rig.hal end block: stepgen.03 gets stepgen.01's [JOINT_1] values, position command and enable

axis3_is_stepgen3.evidence: Faz 3 verification: both Y gantry sides moved about 50 mm

faz2_directions.notes: Positive jog directions observed on the rig. All three SCALE values stay positive.

faz3_scale.notes: SCALE from commanded vs measured moves: new = previous x commanded_mm / measured_mm. The rough round ran on the GRBL-derived values, which were about 8.3x (X, Y) and 10.2x (Z) too high - they were never calibrated for these mechanics. Gate 3: within 1 %. Y was verified on both gantry sides (two motors, one joint).

speeds.notes: Final INI values, raised on 2026-11-12 once SCALE was measured (from 3 mm/s and 10 mm/s^2). Why: with the old SCALE the rig had physically run at about 9 mm/s and about 84 mm/s^2 all day, and a homing search at 5 mm/s stops in 0.25 mm at 50 mm/s^2, against about 1.3 mm of switch overtravel. FERROR / MIN_FERROR raised tenfold: with the measured SCALE one step is about 0.01 mm and the old MIN_FERROR (0.005) was below it. Step timing unchanged: a runtime test with longer pulses changed nothing.

previous.source: configs/test-rig/test-rig.ini as committed before 2026-11-12 (commit 94ede96), same on all three joints unless split

speeds.homing_stop_basis: v^2 / (2 a) at 5 mm/s and 50 mm/s^2

faz4_travel.notes: Each axis was jogged onto its switches before homing; trip points are in the session frame, in which the table is at about 0. The machine frame puts the origin at the home switch's latch release edge (HOME_OFFSET 0). The release edges were estimated by polling and include its latency; homing later showed only small switch hysteresis (Z trip to release about 0.06 mm). Every soft limit is at least 3.3 mm inside a switch trip or the table. The Y two-side racking check was deferred.

faz5_switches.notes: Nets at configs/test-rig/test-rig.hal:301-327. Inputs idle HIGH and read LOW when pressed, so the nets use .in_not. With the machine ON, each switch pressed by hand tripped 'joint N on limit switch error' with N = error_joint. The machine refuses to enable while a joint rests on a limit. LinuxCNC 2.9 clears Override Limits as soon as motion is next in position, so recovering from a limit needs an immediate jog off.

faz6_homing.notes: Home All runs Z -> Y -> X. Single joint: Machine -> Homing -> Home <axis>, or select the axis and press the Home key; the Manual-tab button is Home All. Repeatability is read from joint.N.motor-offset, because the DRO always reads HOME after homing. Before an intermittent X motor-cable contact was repaired, X drifted one way (lost steps); after the repair 0.0017 mm.

faz7_soft_limits.notes: MDI moves beyond the soft limits, all at F300, were rejected by motion and no axis moved.
messages: Linear move on line N would exceed joint J's positive/negative limit

faz8_first_program.notes: A 50 mm square at F300 from X10 Y10, cut in the air. Z moves use G53: the G54 offsets are zero and the Z window is -96.5..-3, so a 'G0 Z5' would be refused. Accepted with an open item: after 3 runs the homing motor-offsets showed Z drifting slightly in one direction, about 0.02 mm per run. Suspected cause: Z acceleration 50 mm/s^2 too high against gravity. Work item: try 25 mm/s^2 and repeat.
faz8_first_program.open_item: Z drift: try MAX_ACCELERATION 25 mm/s^2 on Z and repeat the runs

operations.notes: Session findings that are not measurements of the machine.

orphaned_shm.symptom: after a TERM shutdown the next start fails: AXIS 'A configuration error is preventing LinuxCNC from starting' (s.joints timeout)
orphaned_shm.fix: with no LinuxCNC process running, ipcrm that segment before starting; done by deploy/kiosk-session, which runs deploy/kiosk.sh clean-shm before every LinuxCNC start

boot_after_power_cut.notes: After a building power cut the PC boots usably only in GRUB failsafe mode. In normal mode the screen goes black after the desktop background; the persistence (/dev/sda2, ext3) is clean. The monitor is on the AMD iGPU (HDMI); an NVIDIA GA102 is also present. Failsafe latency beat the earlier normal-mode multi-core value; opening Firefox on the single core raised it.
boot_after_power_cut.failsafe_kernel_params: noapic noapm nodma nomce nosmp nosplash vga=788

network.notes: The USB Wi-Fi dongle drops often and the PC's address changed. The access point rewrites client MACs, so ARP cannot identify the PC: use the hostname 'debian'.

hal_warnings.notes: Printed at every LinuxCNC start, successful starts included. Cause unknown, apparently harmless.

open_items: Wi-Fi dongle reliability, or wired LAN
UI defects and an observer mode
BIOS / latency tuning (failsafe parameters gave better latency)
the kiosk is not installed yet
